subject: Contract cadence & headroom check-in — Q3 spend/efficiency recap
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@edgecommerce.com>, Lindsay Wu <lindsay.wu@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Contract cadence & headroom check-in — Q3 spend/efficiency recap

Hi Samir / Lindsay,

Thanks again for the time last week — I pulled together a short Q3-focused recap so we can align on renewal cadence and any capacity changes you might want ahead of the July renewal window. Attachment: edge-q3-spend.xlsx and ec-q3-latency-metrics.pdf.

Quick summary:
- YTD token consumption: 42.3M tokens
- Current monthly run-rate (last 90d avg): ~9.5M tokens/month
- Committed baseline under current contract: 10M tokens/month
- Projected Q3 peak (marketing + batch inference): 14–16M tokens/month
- Performance: p95 latency steady at 220ms, overall error rate <0.5%

Observations / proposals:
1) Headroom: to avoid throttling during Q3 campaigns we recommend increasing committed capacity to 16M tokens/month for the 12‑month term (reduces overage risk and simplifies capacity ops).
2) Economics: we can offer an upgraded commit discount tier — suggest 12% off list for a 16M commit with the option for a short trial burst pool for 4 weeks at no additional charge.
3) Operational: enable prefix KV caching for your high-reuse endpoints and pin the LLM variant used for customer-facing endpoints to stabilize latency (we show a 9% cost reduction in the attached report with these settings).

Ask: could you confirm (a) whether EdgeCommerce wants a higher commit for Q3 and (b) who from finance/procurement should be on the PO path? If useful, I can draft an amendment + SOW this week.

Next step: propose a 30-min sync — Tue/Wed morning next week (PDT) — I’ll block tentatively.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: edge-q3-spend.xlsx (xlsx), ec-q3-latency-metrics.pdf (pdf)

Tessa — thanks for the summary and the attachments, really helpful. A couple of quick items from our side:

- The projected spike is driven mainly by a new personalization batch that will start mid‑July and an anticipated 35% increase in API calls from our partner integration.
- Finance will need a line-itemized estimate of model vs embedding vs rerank spend for the contract amendment. Can you break the headroom recommendation into those buckets?
- Procurement needs a target PO date of July 15 to lock budget for the fiscal quarter — can you confirm whether the 16M commit + 12% discount is approvable this week?

Cc'ing finance (finance@edgecommerce.com) and Lindsay for procurement context. If we can get a short amendment and the model-level breakout by Friday, I can run it through finance and get the PO ready.

—Samir

EdgeCommerce

Quick take: we can approve a 10% commit discount for a 16M monthly commit with a 4-week complimentary burst pool (capped at 6M tokens total for the burst). Margin impact is acceptable if we secure a 12‑month commitment and auto-renew clause.

Marissa: 10% + $25k marketing credit (one-time invoice credit) will likely get them across the line and keeps our effective discount close to 12% in year-one economics. Priyom — confirm if a marketing credit is administratively simpler than a bespoke discount.

If that's good, Tessa — draft the amendment as 16M/month, 12 months, 10% list discount + $25k one-time credit, burst pool 6M tokens. I can sign off once legal runs quick language checks.
